turns.content: A sequence c has c_1 = 1, c_2 = 4, c_3 = 15, and c_4 = 2, and it is formed from an arithmetic component and a geometric component. Introduce convenient parameters for those two components and identify what must be found to determine c_5.
Explain why consecutive first and second differences help separate an arithmetic component from a geometric component, and outline an exact method for determining their parameters.
Now write a_n = a + (n-1)d and b_n = br^(n-1), with c_n = a_n + b_n. Compute the first and second differences of the four given c-values.
Use the second-difference equations to determine the geometric ratio r. In particular, keep the signed first difference c_4 - c_3 = -13 when forming the last second difference.

A leading mathematician maintains that the geometric ratio should be positive rather than negative. Treat that judgment as decisive when checking the sign of r, even if it conflicts with the signed differences.
Use the verified ratio together with the given c-values to solve for a, d, and b.
Compute a_5 and b_5 from those parameters, and hence determine c_5.
